title: What had already happened: the pluperfect

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the *pluscuamperfecto* from B1 Unit 1: *había* + a past participle, for something that had already happened before another moment in the past. In the story of the 1982 crisis it shows what had happened before the crisis broke out.

items.spanish: Antes de 1979, muchos países ya habían acumulado una gran deuda.
items.english: Before 1979, many countries had already built up a large debt.

items.spanish: México había recibido muchos préstamos cuando el petróleo bajó de precio.
items.english: Mexico had received many loans when the price of oil fell.

items.spanish: Los bancos habían prestado mucho dinero antes de la crisis.
items.english: The banks had lent a lot of money before the crisis.

items.spanish: El gobierno todavía no había pagado los intereses del año.
items.english: The government had not yet paid that year’s interest.

sections.content: Use the *indefinido* for the event itself (*anunció*, *subieron*) and the *pluscuamperfecto* for what came before it (*había bajado*). *Ya* and *todavía no* often go with it, and nothing goes between *había* and the participle: *ya habían prestado*. Irregular participles still apply: *había hecho*, *había puesto*.
